method_selection.citation: Wu et al., Stochastic Shared Embeddings, NeurIPS 2019; adaptive sparse-embedding regularization literature.
method_selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 3.5 and then declines while training loss continues improving, indicating mild overfitting. On this small, sparse-ID dataset, frequency-adaptive embedding regularization directly targets memorization in rare user/item rows and can be tested as one attributable change on the accepted frozen stack. It is untried, low-to-medium cost, and scientifically preferable to another compound sweep. The expected gain is honestly small and may be below the 0.002 convergence threshold, so it should retain half-epoch checkpointing and use matched seeds for confirmation.

rejected.reason: The accepted parent already came from a broad package search; another compound sweep would repeat the opening and would not resolve component attribution.
An ensemble-design direction was already tried and rejected on this dataset, and the single-model intervention should be stabilized before another expensive close.
It is a measured win but has already been tested on this benchmark and primarily treats metric mismatch rather than the observed post-peak overfitting.

expected_delta_basis: Wu et al. (NeurIPS 2019) and adaptive sparse-embedding regularization report consistent small gains from sharing or more strongly shrinking rare embeddings, while the selector notes this treatment is untried but may remain below the 0.002 noise threshold.

hypothesis: Because validation peaks near epoch 3.5 and then declines, the frozen DCN-lite stack is mildly overfitting; an ESMM-style bundle of low-weight training-only auxiliary heads for click, available social outcomes, and multiple watch-ratio thresholds will regularize its shared representation and improve validation primary by at least 0.002.

+def make_pairs(users, labels, seed):

method_selection.citation: ESMM-style multi-task (Ma et al., SIGIR 2018; explicitly endorsed by the brief's appendix A.3); observed working in a public Track 2 solution (github.com/9irija/TikTok_TechJam: DeepFM + 4 social heads, +0.0030 primary, 3-seed verified) — public solutions are in-scope per the resource policy.
method_selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 3.5 and then declines while training loss continues improving, indicating mild overfitting. The current regularized package is already strong, and inverse-frequency embedding regularization failed, so a materially different regularizer is appropriate. A low-weight bundle of training-only auxiliary heads can constrain sparse ID representations through correlated supervision; click auxiliary supervision has also been measured live on this full package. The gain is uncertain and likely small, but this card has plausible >0.002 upside and is more likely to break the convergence streak than another minor schedule or ensemble tweak.

rejected.reason: The immediately preceding node tested inverse-frequency adaptive embedding L2 and fell to 0.6012, so repeating this mechanism would ignore a direct failure.
An ensemble-design sweep was already tried and rejected; its expected gain is below the 0.002 convergence threshold, and member quality has not changed enough to justify repeating it now.

Although measured strong elsewhere, it primarily treats metric mismatch, whereas the observed learning-curve shape directly diagnoses overfitting; the auxiliary-head bundle better matches the present failure mode.

expected_delta_basis: Ma et al. (SIGIR 2018) motivates jointly trained auxiliary tasks, and the selected method card reports a 3-seed-verified +0.0030 primary for a four-social-head DeepFM package, although the fast-path export limits this test mainly to click and play-time-derived heads.
